notes:
Executive summary:
- Customer: Summit Fintech (global payments platform). Strong need: deterministic latency and predictable unit cost for customer-facing chat & fraud-reranking flows.
- Primary ask: dedicated capacity with throughput guarantees and a commercial model for reserved GPU commits (monthly/annual). Also needs EU data residency for some customers.

Technical targets (stated by Summit):
- Chat gen: 1k concurrent sessions, 120 requests/sec steady, p95 latency <= 150ms for short-turn chat (prompt+50 tokens).
- Reranking: 200 qps, p95 latency <= 60ms.
- Embeddings: background batch generation 5M embeddings/day, not latency sensitive but throughput heavy.

Reserved capacity & cost modelling notes (workshop 2026-02-17):
- Proposed reserved footprint (initial): 8x H100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool. Autoscale burst to on-demand for 2x capacity for 30% of peak minutes.
- Model mix assumption: 60% requests served by a quantized 30B chat model (for most flows), 30% by a trimmed 70B variant for high-quality responses, 10% heavy rerank/embedding jobs on specialized kernels.
- Utilization assumption: engineering used a conservative 55% average util across the month to account for diurnal peaks and reserved headroom; finance ran sensitivity at 40%, 55%, 75%.
- Unit economics (internal calc, approximate):
  * On-demand blended inference cost (cloud + runtime) estimate: $1.60 per 1M tokens.
  * Reserved capacity blended cost (8xH100 commit @55% util): $0.48 per 1M tokens.
  * Break-even util to beat on-demand given committed price = ~28% util for the 8x commit size.
- Monthly token volume target (customer forecast): 1.2B tokens/month (chat + rerank + upkeep). At 1.2B tokens: reserved @55% => ~ $576/month per 1M? (note: keep shorthand) -- finance will recalc in formal sheet.

SLA & throughput guarantees discussed:
- Redwood to commit p95 latency SLOs by route: chat p95 <= 150ms (short prompt), rerank p95 <= 60ms. SLA credits to be linear with minutes of breach beyond 1% monthly. Summit prefers uptime SLA >= 99.9% for dedicated pool.
- Fallback policy: auto-route to on-demand compatible model variant on capacity exhaustion. Summit requests automatic circuit-breaker + early-warning telemetry to ops and 30-min manual escalation window.

Negotiation levers and asks from Summit:
- Wants multi-month ramp: Q1 initial 8x commit -> Q3 potential double commit if quality/latency holds. Requests sliding scale discounts for 12-month commit.
- Data residency: require EU region for EU customers; Redwood private control plane or VPC option required for sensitive customers.
- Audit & compliance: want quarterly SOC-like summary and KMS integration for keys.

Open items / actionables:
- Redwood to provide formal cost model spreadsheet (line items: reserved GPU cost, infra overhead, dedicated support, observability retention). Owner: Diego. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Legal: finalize SLA terms and credit formula. Owner: Redwood legal + Summit legal. Target: 2026-03-18.
- Run 7-day high-concurrency load test on a mirrored 8x H100 pool to validate p95 & KVS behavior; schedule week of 2026-03-08.
- Confirm exact H/W equivalence (H100 vs A100) for committed pricing; Summit prefers H100-class.

Quotes or paraphrases captured:
- "Need predictable per-customer unit economics — finance will not accept large variance after we launch pricing tiers." (CTO)
